evals.name: check-is-default-and-read-only
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action): probes Bash 5.0+, jq and node presence, each guard's effective toggle, the cli-flag-verify scan surface, the block-dangerous-git allowlist, and hook registration. Reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table with one remediation line per FAIL. Edits nothing — every tunable is native userConfig.
expectations: Routes to the check action when no argument is given
Reports PASS/FAIL/INFO for Bash, jq, node, and per-guard toggles rather than inventing configuration
Reads the pre-computed node row rather than re-issuing the probe, and reports a missing node as FAIL with the README Requirements remediation
Does not write settings, pluginConfigs, or any consumer-project file during check

evals.name: apply-points-only-never-writes
evals.expected_output: Runs check first, then for each FAIL points at the resolution: platform install guidance for missing jq, missing node, or old Bash, and /plugin configure guardrails (or, headless, a plain claude plugin install ... --config rerun) for toggle or scalar changes. Installs nothing and writes nothing — apply is pure guidance.
expectations: Runs check before offering remediations
Points at /plugin configure, or headless at a plain `claude plugin install guardrails@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config KEY=VALUE` rerun, for toggle changes

Never tells the operator to `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option in the README's Options reference to its manifest default

Cites the marketplace's plugin-reconfiguration convention as the owner of the verified-version record, states the scope rule (pass the scope `claude plugin list` reports for this plugin, `user` from the home directory), says a rejected value still exits 0 so the output is what to read, and defers observation of the new value to rerunning check in a fresh session
Never installs system packages and never writes user settings or pluginConfigs

evals.name: disabled-guards-downgrade-prereq-failures
evals.prompt:
/guardrails:setup check

Every guard toggle is disabled on this machine, and jq and node are missing.
evals.expected_output: When every guard's toggle is disabled, the missing-jq and missing-node prerequisites downgrade from FAIL to INFO — a deliberately disabled plugin is not broken. Reports the probes informationally and notes that re-enabling restores the FAIL semantics.
expectations: Treats missing jq and missing node as INFO rather than FAIL when every guard toggle is disabled
Notes that re-enabling a guard restores the FAIL semantics for prerequisites
Does not claim the plugin is broken solely because jq or node is absent while all guards are off

evals.name: install-git-hooks-is-explicit-only
evals.expected_output: Bare apply installs no git hook. The commit-msg-convention, pre-commit-content and reference-verify entries register only when the explicit `apply install-git-hooks` argument is given.
expectations: Does not run install.mjs copy or write any hook file from bare apply
Names apply install-git-hooks as the action that registers the git-hook entries

evals.name: install-git-hooks-unattended-defaults-to-local
evals.prompt:
/guardrails:setup apply install-git-hooks

Nobody is at this session to answer questions.
evals.expected_output: With no scope argument and nobody to ask, uses scope local: runs install.mjs plan --scope local, then copy --scope local for the copy actions, reasons over each decisions[] item with the git-hook decisions reference, and reports verify's lines. Commits nothing and writes no .githooks/ directory.
expectations: Uses scope local without asking, because no one can answer
Runs plan before copy and applies decisions with its own edit tools rather than expecting the script to
Reports install.mjs verify output at the end
Does not write a shared .githooks/ copy or set core.hooksPath

evals.name: check-reports-retired-commit-msg-hook-guardrails-r001
evals.prompt:
/guardrails:setup check

This clone's .git/hooks/commit-msg is the hook the old `apply install-commit-msg` action installed (its second line reads `# guardrails-commit-msg-convention v1`), with guardrails-resolve-convention.sh beside it.
evals.expected_output: Runs check-retirements.sh against the plugin's retirements.yaml and reports guardrails-r001 as FAIL (a migrate record) and guardrails-r002 as WARN, with apply as the remediation. Changes no file.
expectations: check-retirements.sh is run with --manifest pointing at the plugin's retirements.yaml
guardrails-r001 is reported as FAIL and guardrails-r002 as WARN, each with apply as the remediation
No file is changed by check

evals.name: apply-cleans-retired-resolver-guardrails-r002
evals.prompt:
/guardrails:setup apply

Only .git/hooks/guardrails-resolve-convention.sh is left from the old install-commit-msg action; the operator says yes to every cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs retirement detection, reports guardrails-r002, and after the operator confirms runs check-retirements.sh with --clean guardrails-r002, reports the removed file, then re-runs detection and reports the final state.
expectations: Cleanup of guardrails-r002 runs only after the operator confirms it
Runs check-retirements.sh --clean guardrails-r002 rather than deleting the file by hand
Detection is re-run last and the final state is reported

evals.name: apply-migrates-retired-pre-commit-hook-guardrails-r003
evals.prompt:
/guardrails:setup apply

This clone still has the pre-commit hook the old `apply install-pre-commit-content` action installed, and the user's own earlier hook it chained sits at .git/hooks/pre-commit.pre-guardrails. The operator confirms each step.
evals.expected_output: Reports guardrails-r003 and follows its successor: with the operator confirming, runs --clean guardrails-r003 --i-migrated, moves pre-commit.pre-guardrails back to pre-commit so the user's own hook is kept, and points at apply install-git-hooks to install the pre-commit-content entry, which handles that hook through its foreign-hook decision. Re-runs detection last.
expectations: Runs --clean guardrails-r003 with --i-migrated only after the operator confirms the migrated result
Keeps the user's chained hook by moving .git/hooks/pre-commit.pre-guardrails back to .git/hooks/pre-commit
Points at apply install-git-hooks for the replacement entry rather than installing it from bare apply
The old hook's content is treated as untrusted input and never executed

evals.name: apply-cleans-retired-content-lib-guardrails-r004
evals.prompt:
/guardrails:setup apply

The old pre-commit hook is gone but .git/hooks/guardrails-content-lib/ is still there. The operator says no to the cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Reports guardrails-r004 as WARN, asks before cleaning, and on the operator's no leaves the directory in place and reports it as still present. Never runs --clean guardrails-r004 without a yes.
expectations: guardrails-r004 is reported and its cleanup is offered behind its own confirmation
On the operator's no, check-retirements.sh --clean guardrails-r004 is not run and the directory is left in place
The final report lists guardrails-r004 as still present
